checks.finding: Round 3 added the missing id/name/context regex patterns to REQ-002 and the Field Definitions table, and the accompanying prose (e.g., 'digits and consecutive uppercase letters like APIOrder allowed, no separator chars') removes the two-implementer-divergence risk flagged in earlier rounds. Remaining free-text fields (definition, essence, evidence[], stakeholder_perspectives[].actor/concern, distinguished_from[].reasons[]) are intentionally unconstrained narrative fields with no implied machine-checkable format, so leaving them as plain strings is not an ambiguity. No term, actor, state, input, or output was found where two implementers would reasonably diverge.

The round-2 conflict between Roles and Permissions (which previously implied meta.status Approved writes had some enforcement) and the actual hook-guard scope has been resolved: Roles and Permissions (requirements.md 'meta.status の Approved 書込に対する機械的強制は存在しない...承認境界は人間のレビュー運用のみが担保') now matches the Non-goals bullet added this round ('meta.status の Approved 書込に対する機械的強制機構...の新設') and matches INV-008. Cross-checked contexts/relations, single-context-per-concept vs distinguished_from cross-context references, and the same-context-name-invalid vs cross-context-name-valid rules (Edge Cases) for internal consistency; found no direct conflict between any requirement, acceptance criterion, constraint, or non-goal.

REQ-002 (requirements.md, Field Definitions table) declares seven required concept fields: id, name, context, definition, essence, responsibilities, evidence. AC-014/TEST-014 (acceptance-tests.md) is the only acceptance criterion aimed at required-field enforcement, and it exercises exactly three of the seven ('essence 欠落・evidence 空配列・responsibilities 空配列'); id/name/context are exercised only for pattern violation while present (AC-018), never for outright key absence, and 'definition' has no negative fixture anywhere in the table -- its required-ness is never verified by any AC/TEST. Downstream failure mode: an implementer building validate-domain-contract.sh/.ps1 and the REQ-006 drift-lock suite from this table alone could ship a validator that silently accepts a concept missing 'definition' (or missing id/name/context keys outright), and no fixture in REQ-005/REQ-006 would catch it -- the task author decomposing REQ-005(d) would follow the same table and inherit the same gap. This belongs to spec review because it is a completeness gap in acceptance-tests.md itself, not an implementation choice, and it directly undercuts Risk R2's claim (requirements.md) that REQ-006 fixtures fully drift-lock the schema's required/pattern declarations against validator behavior -- that claim is not true for the 'definition' field or for outright key-absence on id/name/context. Severity is Major per calibration ('missing observable acceptance criterion' for a field the spec itself declares required), not Critical because it is not a safety/workflow-boundary contradiction, and not Minor because it leaves a stated required-field rule completely unverified rather than merely under-clarified.

The three listed Assumptions (hook-runtime-unavailable deviation, v1-instances-do-not-exist per owner decision INV-009, and future-phase non-modification contingency) are each explicitly resolved with recorded owner decisions or contingency plans. Investigation.md's OQ-001..OQ-004 retain 'Status: Open' labels, but each is functionally resolved in the body text this round: OQ-002 (CI/run-all registration) defaults to no additional work and requirements.md contains no conflicting CI-registration requirement; OQ-003 (essence required) is adopted directly in REQ-002 and the Field Definitions table; OQ-004 (v1 rejection behavior) is adopted directly in REQ-004(b) and tested by AC-012; OQ-001 (v1 schema file disposition) is explicitly deferred to a future Phase 3 and is outside this feature's Non-goals-bounded scope, so it does not block Phase 0 design/task decomposition. The stale 'Open' labels in investigation.md and the generic 'spec-review までに人間が確定する' sentence in requirements.md's Open Questions section are leftover boilerplate rather than unresolved decisions, since the operative requirements already encode the answers.

A governance boundary is in scope: contracts carry meta.status including an 'Approved' value. Requirements.md now states plainly and consistently (Roles and Permissions, reinforced by the new Non-goals bullet) that no mechanical enforcement of Approved-status writes exists or is being added in this feature, and that the boundary is purely a human review process outside this feature's scope. Because the spec does not claim any automated approval gate while treating meta.status as 'a plain enumerated-value field' (tested structurally via AC-001's meta-shape check against v1), there is no untested or falsely-implied enforcement mechanism -- the one thing this feature builds around the boundary (the field's presence/shape) is observable and tested.

Requirements.md gives REQ-001..007 with a full Field Definitions table, explicit validator check list (a)-(i) in REQ-004, Roles and Permissions, Main Workflows, Edge Cases, Security Boundaries, and Risks with mitigations; acceptance-tests.md maps every REQ-004 check letter and REQ-005 fixture category to a numbered AC/TEST. A design reviewer for implementation-policy review would not need to invent product behavior for schema shape, validator error surface, fixture corpus composition, or non-regression guarantees for v1. The single coverage gap identified under EDGE-CASE-COVERAGE (definition-field required-ness untested) is a missing acceptance-test fixture, not an invented-product-behavior problem -- REQ-002 already states the behavior unambiguously, so it does not block handoff readiness on its own.
